name: roofs_mixed_b
prompt:
Image 1 is the finished sheet; image 2 is its layout: 9 building outlines seen from above on flat magenta, in a 3×3 grid. Redraw only cells 1, 3 and 7 (the transparent areas). Keep every other cell exactly as it is, and match their style, colours and fine detail.

The faults in those cells:
- Cell 1: the onion dome was drawn from the side — its drum, bulb and cross standing up like a picture of a church. Looking straight down, an onion dome is a round gilded circle about 2.5 m across (about 87 px here) with a bright highlight towards the top-left, a small dark ring of drum around it, and the cross seen from above as a thin small cross at its centre, about 30 px long. The chapel's green gabled roof stays as it was, with its ridge along the long axis.
- Cells 3 and 7: each was drawn as a gable with a ridge down the middle. They are lean-to roofs: one single slope with no ridge, its sheets or slates running from the high back edge down to the street edge, shaded evenly from one side to the other.

For each redrawn cell, trace the outline in image 2 exactly, keep its proportions, straight square edges, top-down with no perspective, and keep the magenta background flat pure #FF00FF outside it. No text.

1. 9.4 × 6.1 m (1.5× wider than deep) — small Orthodox chapel, gabled roof of green sheet metal with one gilded onion dome and a cross
3. 3.9 × 6.5 m (1.7× deeper than wide) — small yard outbuilding or shed, lean-to roof of grey asbestos-cement slate, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall
7. 3.2 × 7.8 m (2.4× deeper than wide) — small yard outbuilding or shed, lean-to roof of corrugated metal, standing narrow end to the street with the entrance on that short front wall
